title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 59
paragraphs: Having said this, he led the Persians on at a run, after they had crossed the Asopos, on the track of the Greeks, supposing they were running away from him; and he directed his attack against the Lacedaemonians and Tegeans only, not seeing the Athenians, whose march was toward the plain, because of the hills. The rest of the barbarian division commanders, seeing that the Persians had set off in pursuit of the Greeks, all at once raised the signals for battle and began to pursue, each as fast as they could, with no order or sequence of posts.
